chunks: Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Khālid, from Abī al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام; and Ṣabbāḥ al-Ḥadhdhāʾ, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī Ibrāhīm Mūsā عليه السلام: concerning

About a man who approaches a beast sexually, they all said: “If the beast belongs to the perpetrator, it is to be slaughtered; then when it dies, it is to be burned with fire, and no benefit is to be taken from it. And he is to be struck with twenty-five lashes, one quarter of the hadd of the fornicator. If the beast does not belong to him, it is to be appraised, its price taken from him and given to its owner, and it is to be slaughtered and burned with fire, and no benefit is to be taken from it, and he is to be struck with twenty-five lashes.”

So I said: “What is the fault of the beast?” He said: “It has no fault, but the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم did this and commanded it, so that people would not suffice themselves with beasts and the progeny would not be cut off.”

key_terms.الْبَهِيمَةُ: a beast or animal involved in the ruling
key_terms.حَدِّ الزَّانِي: the legal punishment of the fornicator, used here as a measure
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose practice is cited as precedent

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām on a man who has intercourse with a beast?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who commits an act with a beast, detailing the punishment and the disposal of the animal. It also explains that the animal bears no guilt; rather, the ruling was enacted by the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as a deterrent so that people would not turn to such acts and thereby disrupt human progeny.
